ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Sonny Liston Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Establishing care: a high blood pressure reading at a boxing commission check, trauma-informed history, alcohol and drug screening with a safety assessment, and health literacy. Concerns: He wants to keep fighting and needs his blood pressure under control to pass the commission physical; He wants things explained to him out loud, not handed to him on paper; He knows he drinks too much between fights and wants to cut down without being lectured. [S]

tr.td: Twelve-lead ECG: sinus bradycardia at 56 per minute; voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy without repolarization changes; normal intervals (PR 168 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc 402 ms)
24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: daytime average 146/94 mmHg, nighttime average 132/84 mmHg, 24-hour average 142/91 mmHg; nighttime fall 10 percent; confirms hypertension

Transthoracic echocardiogram: mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (septum and posterior wall 12 mm), normal chamber size, ejection fraction 60 percent, normal diastolic function (septal e' 10 cm/s), normal valves, aortic root 34 mm
Tdap vaccine; no record of an earlier tetanus booster
Hepatitis B vaccine (HepB-CpG), dose 1 of 2, recommended for all adults 19 to 59

list.item: Professional heavyweight boxer, still competing and training six days a week; married; lives in Las Vegas [S]
Grew up on a farm with many brothers and sisters; did field work from childhood and had almost no schooling; does not read or write and asks that forms and instructions be read to him [S]
Spent about two years in a state prison as a young man, where he learned to box; he chose to share this and said it was where his life turned [S]
Alcohol: vodka or beer most days, usually two or three drinks and five to six on weekend nights (about 25 drinks a week); has tried to cut down before training camps [S]
No opioid, stimulant, cannabis or sedative use, no injection drug use (DAST-10 0); does not smoke [S]
Health literacy: answers "always" to needing help reading health materials; strong memory for spoken instructions and demonstrations [S]
Strengths and supports: discipline and daily training, physical strength, a sharp memory, his family, his trainer and gym, and the steadiness he says boxing gave him [S]

tr.td: Establishing care: a high blood pressure reading at a boxing commission check, trauma-informed history, alcohol and drug screening with a safety assessment, and health literacy
Two-week review, seen the same day by cardiology: ambulatory monitoring, echocardiogram, the diagnosis and treatment, and fitness to compete
Four-week review: blood pressure on treatment, potassium and creatinine, drinking, and medicine teach-back
Three-month review: blood pressure, liver tests and drinking on naltrexone
Four-month review: blood pressure at goal, AUDIT, and the plan ahead
Same-day sick visit for a cold and raised blood pressure

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Confirm the blood pressure out of the office with 24-hour ambulatory monitoring before any diagnosis or medicine; baseline metabolic panel, glucose, lipids, urine albumin, TSH and ECG
Cardiology consultation on the same day as the two-week visit: confirm and stage the hypertension, echocardiogram, choice of treatment, and fitness to compete

Alcohol: nonjudgmental brief intervention with motivational interviewing; a drinking goal he sets himself; medicines (naltrexone, acamprosate or topiramate) explained; AUDIT-C at each follow-up and liver tests
Safety plan given out loud and as a picture card, with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline saved in his phone as a voice contact; safety reviewed at every visit

Health literacy universal precautions at every visit: plain spoken explanations, one or two key points at a time, teach-back, a picture-based medicine and blood pressure card, consent forms read aloud with time for questions, phone and voice-message reminders instead of letters, and an adult literacy program offered without pressure
Trauma-informed care: an ACE-informed history in which he chooses what to share, explanation and permission before each part of the examination, a PTSD screen, and counseling offered
Drug use screening with the DAST-10; naloxone and overdose education if any opioid use is reported or suspected

Start a single-pill combination of amlodipine 5 mg and valsartan 160 mg each morning for stage 2 hypertension; potassium and creatinine in two to four weeks; home blood pressure with a talking, large-display monitor; lower-salt eating and alcohol reduction
Competing: no bouts until blood pressure is controlled, then clearance by the commission physician with a repeat check; no stimulants, decongestants or weight-cut diuretics
Raise the combination to amlodipine 10 mg and valsartan 160 mg; start naltrexone 50 mg each morning, with a wallet card saying it blocks opioid pain medicines and a liver test recheck in two months
Cardiovascular risk and preventive care at the preventive visit: lipids, risk estimate, immunizations and one-time screenings
Confirm or rule out hypertension with out-of-office readings before any medicine
Ambulatory monitoring confirmed stage 2 hypertension (daytime 146/94 mmHg)
Blood pressure under 130/80 mmHg in the clinic and at home by four months
Clinic 122/76 mmHg; home average 120/76 mmHg on amlodipine 10 mg and valsartan 160 mg
Drink within the goal he set: no more than 14 drinks a week and no more than 4 on any day, and none in the two weeks before a fight
About 8 drinks a week with no day above 3; AUDIT 7; GGT normal
Explain his medicines and blood pressure plan back in his own words
Teach-back correct at four weeks with the picture card

list.item: Fully independent; trains six days a week (roadwork, bag and sparring); no limitation from the old shoulder or jaw injuries [S]

Alert, watchful at first and then relaxed once he was told what each step of the visit would be; speaks briefly and to the point; mood "all right"; no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone; no psychotic symptoms; insight good about drinking before fights [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1969-06-09: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with a spoken and picture-based safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline saved in his phone by voice contact, and a two-week follow-up; safety reviewed at every visit [S]
